summary: Nora tidies her own notebook: questions that have been answered or overtaken stop appearing, and notes about the same occasion can be combined.
details: A note whose occasion has passed, where the body shows the question was answered or can no longer be answered, stops appearing in what Nora is shown.

Two notes about the same occasion can be combined into one that keeps everything both said, including any disagreement — the surviving note is the older, and the other is retired pointing at it. A combined note that came back SHORTER than the longest note it was meant to keep is rejected, because that is a summary and something was dropped.
A group Nora asked to combine is never taken apart note by note instead. If the combination does not go through for any reason, both notes stay exactly as they were.
limitations: COMBINING NOTES DOES NOT HAPPEN YET, and this is the honest version of a claim an earlier draft of this note got wrong. Two notes count as the same occasion only when they share a date AND resolve to the same people in the shared registry of who's who — and nothing in the system fills that registry in for notes yet. So every candidate pair is refused today. The alternative was to match on the words the model itself typed, which is worse in both directions: three spellings of one wedding read as three different occasions, while two unrelated notes that both say 「wedding」 read as one and would be combined irreversibly. The refusals are counted, so the number says what filling in the registry would unlock.
Off by default and behind three separate switches; nothing is combined or retired until an operator turns the background pass on for a room.
Nothing is deleted — a retired note stays readable, it just stops appearing in what Nora is shown.
